newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary fin.min urges energy price scheme revision.
newsitem.headline: Hungary fin.min urges energy price scheme revision.

text.p: Hungary should revise its energy price hike mechanism to reduce inflationary effects and ensure appropriate return to investors in the energy industry, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Wednesday.
"An agreement should be reached, which would guarantee the return on investments and at the same time exclude elements which generate inflation unnecessarily," he told a conference of businessmen.
Western investors, including German, French, Belgian aand Italian companies, bought large stakes in Hungary's gas and electricity distribution firms and power plants in 1995.
They undertook to spend billions of dollars for technological development while the government promised to ensure eight percent return on their investments from 1997.

However, the investors expressed their dissatisfaction over price hikes introduced on January 1 and urged the government to change the energy price rise mechanism, in which the prices are revised quarterly according to a complicated formula.
Medgyessy said investors' concerns might be justified.
"It would be silly to think that energy production and distribution companies will accept that their investments will not yield a return," he said.

He added that the price formula itself needed correction, as it linked price hikes to the change of industrial prices which also included energy prices and so created a circle of inflation generation.
Medgyessy mentioned energy prices as a key element in the ministry's anti-inflationary plans which he first outlined at the conference.

Energy prices do not represent a large percentage of the consumer price index basket, but the psychological effect of energy price hikes is large in Hungary, where high inflation expectations are the motor of price rises, the minister added.

Urged by the International Monetary Fund to take drastic measures, the Finance Ministry is working on plans which it expects will reduce inflation to single-digit figures in 1998 from a forecast 16-18 percent in 1997.
